newsitem.title: UK: Gold Outlook - Further consolidation seen for gold.
newsitem.headline: Gold Outlook - Further consolidation seen for gold.

text.p: A sliver of confidence helped brace the precious metals markets last week as dealers decided prices had seen their lows for the moment.
"There seems to be support at $368 per ounce (for gold) and that is encouraging people to be a little more positive," one dealer said.
But that did not imply gold had the impetus to drag the rest of the complex much higher before the end of the year, he added.
"If we see $370-$371 that will be it for the rest of the year," he forecast.
At last week's close gold was fairly comfortable at $369.30/$369.80, its highest London finish in a week spent in a range of barely $1.50.
Dealers and analyst were looking for further consolidation this week as the markets recovered from three-year lows plumbed by gold, platinum and palladium in late November.
Silver showed a little more resilience early this month when it found a floor at a 21-month low.
"We're looking for gold to trade between $368-$370 for the next couple of days. There's just not a lot going on as people want to be square towards the end of the year," a dealer said.
Tony Warwick-Ching, metals analyst with research group CRU International, saw a similar situation continue through into the new year.
"Silver and platinum continue to be dampened by what is happening in gold. Neither one is fundamentally strong enough to pull out from that," he said.
Gold prices have been struggling since early November as the market has tried to cope with the phantom of at least one central bank selling gold from reserves.
Dealers said rumours suggested a 10-million ounce sale had been trickling on to the market over the past several weeks.
"There has been a lot of selling from a lot of different directions. It could be a bank, but not necessarily," an analyst said.
Producers from Australia and South Africa selling metal to protect their profit margins against falling prices had added a more direct physical pressure to the price level.

"Against an oversold background, prices are managing to hold over the lows and there are some signs the downtrend is slowing down," technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary.
"However, there are no indications of any worthwhile corrective strenth emerging and further falls continue likely in due course," she added.
Silver closed Friday at $4.82/$4.84, slightly firmer with gold.
Platinum was about 80 cents ahead at $368.55/$369.55 but palladium met some dealer selling and was shown at $117.75/$118.75, down a dollar.
